body_markdown:
# Daily Loop-Model Briefing - 2026-10-21

## Outcome

Five papers were added, and each reuses a learned block inside one forward pass. Two are
design papers for looped language models: PAR supervises each iteration to advance the
state by a fixed amount, and AsymLoop splits the stack into a once-run encoder and a looped
decoder. The other three apply or study existing looped models: histology-based gene
expression prediction, clinical text processing with Ouro and HRM-Text, and a probing study
of what Ouro's loops compute.

Two additions cite Benhao Huang's work.
[Asymmetric Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28489) cites Towards Looped
Models Done Right, Part I as related work, for how recurrence can be organized across layer
topologies and for controlled comparisons where partial looping beats full-stack looping.
[Present but Hard to Read](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28498) cites Towards Looped Models
Done Right, Part II as related work, for reading Huginn's states as approaching fixed points
while Ouro's do not.

## Added

### PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
[arXiv:2610.27628](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27628)

**TL;DR:** Training iteration k to predict the state after the first k operations, and
keeping the recurrent state at a fixed scale, lets a looped model track state far beyond its
training length: 95.5% at 16 times the training length on swap-S5.

- **Setup:** Qwen2.5-0.5B is retrofitted into a prelude (layers 1–8), a weight-tied core
  (layers 9–16) and a coda (layers 17–24). Tasks are synthetic state tracking: S5 and A5
  word problems, swap-S5, rule-table chains and graph reachability. Scaling runs use Qwen2.5
  up to 7B and Qwen3 up to 4B.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Each iteration's prediction is supervised against the state
  after the first k operations. After every iteration, each token's state is rescaled to its
  first-iteration RMS norm. The coda also learns a completion readout that decides when to
  answer, and prefix self-distillation replaces step labels with final answers on shorter
  prefixes.
- **Results:** On swap-S5 at 512 moves, accuracy is 95.5%, against 55.7% reported for RLT
  and 0.8% for explicit chain of thought. With the learned halting readout it is 92.9%,
  against 93.2% with an oracle stopping depth. Without norm anchoring the extrapolation
  factor falls from 16 times to below 2.2 times.
- **Caveat:** Only algorithmic or templated state-tracking tasks are tested, graph
  reachability does not extrapolate, and seed variance on larger backbones is large.
- **Why added:** A training recipe and halting readout for a weight-tied recurrent core,
  aimed at extrapolating recurrent depth to longer problems.

### Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
[arXiv:2610.28489](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28489)

**TL;DR:** AsymLoop encodes the context once and loops only a weight-tied decoder that
attends to the encoder's fixed key-value caches, beating full-stack looping at matched
effective depth from 60M to 1B parameters.

- **Setup:** LLaMA-style models at 60M, 135M, 350M and 1B, trained from scratch on
  FineWeb-Edu at Chinchilla budgets. Evaluation covers validation perplexity and seven
  commonsense benchmarks, with extra runs on an OLMo-style backbone, a sparse MoE variant
  and GSM8K fine-tuning.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Half of the layers form a causal encoder that runs once and
  produces per-layer global KV caches, which stay fixed across iterations. The other half
  form a weight-tied decoder that runs K times and attends jointly to the global KV and to
  local KV from its own evolving state, under one softmax. A heavy-tail-guided layerwise
  learning rate is used for training.
- **Results:** At 1B, average zero-shot accuracy rises from 49.58% for Full Loop to 50.85%
  (49.31% for the unlooped model). At 350M, perplexity is 12.00 at K=3, against 12.30 for
  Full Loop at the same effective depth.
- **Caveat:** AsymLoop costs more training compute than Full Loop, and a FLOP-matched,
  wider Full Loop closes about 40% of the gap. Part of the gain comes from the layerwise
  learning-rate method rather than the architecture.
- **Why added:** A loop-topology design that separates once-run context encoding from a
  weight-tied recurrent decoder.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I, cited twice in the
  introduction as related work on loop topologies and on partial looping beating full-stack
  looping in controlled comparisons.

### HistoLoop: Iterative Contextual Inference with a Looped Transformer for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
[arXiv:2610.28339](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28339)

**TL;DR:** A looped Transformer refines per-spot states over four coarse-to-fine steps with
a shared spatial Transformer and retrieval module, and reaches the best average score on
HEST-Bench gene expression prediction.

- **Setup:** Gene expression prediction from frozen UNI features of H&E images on HEST-1K,
  over six cancer types in five organs, scored by HVG50 gene-wise Pearson correlation over
  five seeds. The model has 674.8M parameters and runs four refinement steps.
- **Mechanism / Method:** At each step, the current spot states are pooled into context
  tokens at a finer resolution, processed by a shared spatial Transformer, and read back
  through a shared cross-attention module. A memory-mediated update writes the result into
  persistent spot states. Resolution embeddings and memory routers are step-specific.
- **Results:** Macro HVG50 correlation is 0.480, against 0.435 for MoLF and 0.405 for
  STFlow. Removing the loop gives 0.381, and a parameter-matched model without the loop
  gives 0.386.
- **Caveat:** It is evaluated on one benchmark, the loop is short and changes resolution at
  every step, and there is no study of more iterations.
- **Why added:** An application of a shared, repeatedly executed Transformer block to a
  scientific vision task, with a parameter-matched unlooped control.

### Exploring Recurrent-Depth Language Models for Multitask Clinical Text Processing
[arXiv:2610.27559](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27559)

**TL;DR:** Fine-tuned jointly on clinical NLP tasks, the looped Ouro-1.4B-Thinking beats
Qwen3-1.7B on 11 of 13 datasets and Ouro-2.6B-Thinking is competitive with Qwen3-8B.

- **Setup:** Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, HRM-Text-1B, Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B
  are fine-tuned on 9 clinical datasets for extraction, classification, inference and
  question answering, and also tested on 4 held-out datasets.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Ouro applies its whole decoder stack four times (its exit gate is
  not used). HRM-Text couples a high-level and a low-level module, each reused across
  recurrent updates. Each recurrent forward pass is trained as one step.
- **Results:** On MedQA, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking scores 0.5075 against 0.4399 for Qwen3-1.7B,
  and Ouro-2.6B-Thinking scores 0.6127 against 0.5734 for Qwen3-8B. On MMLU-Pro Health,
  Ouro-2.6B-Thinking scores 0.5456 against 0.5067 for Qwen3-8B, while HRM-Text-1B scores
  lowest at 0.3123.
- **Caveat:** Pretraining data and compute differ across model families, so, as the
  authors note, the gaps cannot be attributed to recurrence alone. Each setting was trained
  once.
- **Why added:** An application study whose question is whether recurrent-depth language
  models help in a concrete domain.

### Present but Hard to Read: Probing Latent Reasoning with Minimal Pairs
[arXiv:2610.28498](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28498)

**TL;DR:** Minimal-pair probes show that values standard probes miss are present in looped
Ouro-1.4B's state, and patching shows that an intermediate sum readable across loops is not
used for the answer.

- **Setup:** Frozen Ouro-1.4B, read at the middle and end of each of its four loops, and
  Qwen2.5-1.5B as a standard Transformer, on GSM8K-style prompts. The main computation
  studies were pre-registered.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Prompts that differ in one digit are compared to isolate that
  digit's trace. A protocol with a copy ceiling, a prime modulus, all linear combinations of
  the inputs and a synthetic mixing null tests whether a value is computed or merely mixed
  in. Subspace patching and clamping across loops test whether it is used.
- **Results:** A copied digit is read at 0.92–0.97 with minimal pairs in Ouro, against 0.36
  for the best single-prompt probe even after 5,249 training questions. Patching the answer
  at the last loop moves the written digit with a hit rate of 0.902, while patching the
  intermediate a+b gives 0.017.
- **Caveat:** The computed-value signal is small, generic mixing explains much of it, and
  the computation studies cover only Ouro on simple a±b−c problems.
- **Why added:** A mechanistic interpretability study of a looped language model's
  per-loop states.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II (arXiv:2610.06833),
  cited in related work for reading Huginn's states as approaching fixed points while
  Ouro's do not.

## Catalog update

This run checked one fifth of the existing catalog (71 papers) for publication venue,
official code links and community comment links. No entry changed. Some papers state
acceptances in their arXiv comments or journal references, but none could be confirmed
against an official venue page today, and no new official code repository was found.

## Near misses

- **Continuum-LM** ([2610.26959](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26959)): integrates each
  pretrained attention and feed-forward branch with a higher-order ODE solver, so each
  branch is evaluated four times per forward pass. The reuse is local to each sublayer, the
  authors say it is not a parameter-shared neural ODE, and it is held for a maintainer
  decision.
- **Predictive Latents for Autoregressive Language Models**
  ([2610.28540](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28540)): a theory note on iterating a latent
  map over an autoregressive model's hidden state, with recurrent depth as one motivating
  example among several; it analyzes no reused-block architecture.
